angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 991,373 km at 140.24 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.1305 +/- 0.0098 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 140.24 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.425 +/- 0.048 solar radii from Barone et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 28109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...704A..41B/abstract): 991,373 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.227 +/- 0.052 solar masses from Barone et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 28109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...704A..41B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6189 +/- 55 K from Barone et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 28109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...704A..41B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barone et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 28109 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...704A..41B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-28109.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.219, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
